paper.title: A cellular-automata model of flow in ant trails: non-monotonic variation of speed with density
paper.journal: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 35(41):L573-L577

headline: Ant-trail flow CA 2002 (CA, disclosed): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; small f=0.005 rho*=0.55 (band var 0.34) vs large f=0.95 rho*=0.50 (band var 0.35) — pheromone coupling right-shifts the flow peak and evaporation recovers NaSch

verdicts.gate: P1 velocity plateau at small f=0.005: <v> variation across [0.2,0.5] < 0.2
reasons: small-f (f=0.005) velocity variation across [0.2,0.5] = 0.3376 (need < 0.2); band <v> ranges [0.250, 0.378] — the anomaly is a velocity RISE into the near-0.5 peak, which breaks a flat-plateau bar over the locked band; reported honestly, not tuned

verdicts.gate: P2 right-shifted flow peak at small f=0.005: rho* > 0.5
P3 evaporation recovers NaSch at large f=0.95: rho* back toward 0.5 (<= 0.55) AND <v> variation > 0.2

extra.mechanism: pheromone-coupled single-lane exclusion process on a periodic ring (vmax=1, NaSch-like): parallel exclusion hop with a pheromone-dependent hop probability (Q with a mark ahead, q without, q<Q), followed by deposit (mark under each ant) and evaporation (unused marks decay with prob f) — a genuine exclusion process coupled to an evaporating stigmergic field, NOT an agent-stepping ABM
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the anomalous ant-trail fundamental diagram (pheromone coupling right-shifts the flow peak and, as f->1, recovers plain NaSch) and would catch an artifact

citations: Chowdhury, D., Guttal, V., Nishinari, K. & Schadschneider, A. (2002). A cellular-automata model of flow in ant trails: non-monotonic variation of speed with density. Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 35(41):L573-L577. doi:10.1088/0305-4470/35/41/103.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the anomalous ant-trail fundamental diagram (velocity plateau, right-shifted flow peak, and f->1 recovery of plain NaSch)
